findings.reason: the section must name `list_plan_reviews` as the reader the predicate enumerates over (and the gate's existing `read_plan_review(... plan=resource.path)` call at `reckon/crew/routing.py:2698` likewise moved onto that enumeration), or the predicate cannot find the stored `section_digests` it compares against.
findings.text: §16 says the coverage predicate is "one function over two existing readers" and joins "a set of outstanding sections to the union of digests across stored records", but `read_plan_review` returns exactly one record (newest, fingerprint- or version-filtered) and cannot supply a union across records; the only existing reader that enumerates every stored review of a project is `plan_review.list_plan_reviews` (`reckon/crew/plan_review.py:668`), which the section does not name, so the claim that the predicate "adds no walk of its own" is unmet and its dependency set is mis-stated

findings.reason: the section's interface accounting and its `public_definitions` done-when must name the exported card predicate and the raise to +2, or the node's own gate will read as failed when the count moves by two.
findings.text: §17 exports "the one card predicate the parser module exposes beside the identity function" and points `reckon/doccheck.py:116` and `reckon/crew/plan_review.py:208` at it; both consumers sit outside `reckon/_plan_html`, so by §16's stated house rule the predicate is public and counted, yet §17's interface accounting ("one public definition is added, the reader on `reckon/_plan_html.py`") and its done-when ("`public_definitions` at the head is exactly one higher than at the base") count only `plan_headings`, understating the family growth by one
